It is ℂ with the a.e. structure pulled back by J(z) = z + z⁻¹ on ℂ ∖ {0,±1} (devStructure), with G = ⊥ ≤ Perm ℂ. sing = {0,±1} (support_joukowskiStructure). At 0, a chart would equal the unbounded J on a punctured neighbourhood (joukowski_chart_eq), which contradicts continuity. At ±1, a chart would identify z = ±(1+t) with z⁻¹. O = 0 is rigid (joukowski_eq_of_isAEMorphism). The two morphisms agree after J on a portly set. Unboundedness of J at 0 forces f₁(y₀) = 0. J is injective on the punctured unit disc. IsAEMorphism.eq_of_eqOn then concludes, using the connectedness of U₁. `rot` at ±1 is the flip z ↦ z⁻¹ from B(±1,1/2) onto its inverse image, an a.e. isomorphism by J-invariance. Its codomain is connected because it is the image of the ball under inv. It is not the restriction of an automorphism: rigidity at 0 with U = ℂ makes every automorphism the identity, while (5/4)s ≠ ((5/4)s)⁻¹. I re-checked independently that the facts are mathematically right for this structure. With G trivial, φ ∈ {id, inv} locally on the connected regular part, and inv is impossible near 0. So the witness exercises every field and exhibits the cex's distinguishing behaviour: a rigid O next to singular points with non-extendable local isomorphisms. That also discharges AUDIT-2's minor.
